cases.name: protected text and image framing preserves compatibility and default redaction
cases.scenario: Supported clients exchange ordinary and protected text replies and raster images, with and without expiry; malformed, truncated or nested protection frames also arrive. Review framing, ordinary history/search projections and compatibility. This feature controls accidental screen disclosure in supported clients: it is not recipient-resistant encryption, screenshot prevention or secure memory erasure. Do not require resistance to modified recipients, and do not mistake base64 text encoding for encryption. Legacy clients need not reveal protected messages, but ordinary existing wire formats and legacy raw text must remain compatible. Compatibility evidence in this source suite consists of explicit golden ordinary encodings, the reserved outer zero-deadline sentinel and the inspected legacy-expiry decoder fixture. This does not certify arbitrary historical binaries, especially pre-expiry decoders; do not turn absent old binaries into an unsupported claim of universal deployed-client safety.
rubric: Click and authenticate modes survive text/image encoding and decoding without changing the wire encoding of ordinary messages or file manifests.
Protected text is omitted by default history, context and search projection; protected images expose a content-free card without their original filename or ordinary thumbnail content.

Reserved framing is bounded and malformed protected input fails closed without plaintext fallback; legacy raw text that merely resembles a protection magic is not incorrectly consumed as a protected frame.

Expiry coexists with protection, the reserved zero-deadline framing is rejected by the supplied legacy-expiry compatibility fixture, and golden ordinary wire encodings remain unchanged; limitations on historical client behavior are stated without claiming arbitrary pre-expiry binaries were verified.

The documented screen-visibility control, retained encrypted history and existing transport encryption remain distinct; no added protection mode falsely promises cryptographic denial of recipient access.

cases.name: exact retained image reveal has no ordinary media or export bypass
cases.scenario: An authorized desktop asks for one retained protected image while ordinary image APIs, file exports, aliases sharing a transfer identity, recall, expiry, history clearing and disk-restored media are also exercised. Trace the exact reference through canonical retained-history projection and the canonical file manifest into checksum/signature-checked image bytes. The core explicit reveal API delegates local identity authentication to its desktop caller; that delegation is intentional and reviewed separately. The requirement covers supported-client entry points, not modified-client access to recipient plaintext.
rubric: Reveal resolves the exact account/channel message identity and current canonical eligibility; an unrelated, recalled, expired or no-longer-retained message cannot reveal bytes merely because its media file remains cached.

Protection comes from the canonical manifest as well as retained message policy; weaker aliases, missing manifest metadata or ordinary read_media/read_file/save/export paths cannot expose protected image bytes.

Supported protected images are bounded raster images with validated media kind, size, signatures and content integrity; generic files, videos, folders and unsupported formats cannot silently become ordinary sends.

Internal encrypted staging and persistence remain possible without making their privileged byte-assembly route a public ordinary-read bypass; content availability and reveal authorization remain distinct.

Policy and retention are rechecked after potentially expensive image reads so recall/expiry or retirement does not knowingly return stale eligible content; lifecycle and restore behavior preserve the declared protection boundary.

cases.name: desktop reveal reuses app lock with exact session and runtime authority
cases.scenario: A viewer requests one protected text or image, then locks and unlocks, logs out, switches local user, replaces the participant runtime, or recalls/expires the message while the system or password prompt is open. Review both reveal commands and the shared admission/authentication owners. Click mode still requires a valid current session. Authenticate mode must reuse the current app-lock verifier on every reveal: macOS device-owner authentication and the existing non-macOS app-lock password policy. This case assesses source authority and reuse only. Actual OS prompt presentation and physical fingerprint/password acceptance require separate native evidence; their absence is an explicit evidence limit, not a failed source rubric item or a reason to treat a mock as physical acceptance. Any claim that the real prompt was exercised without evidence remains a finding.
rubric: Only explicit nonzero account/channel message references are accepted, and image/text commands cannot reinterpret an arbitrary file identity or legacy device reference as authorized reveal authority.

Authenticate mode invokes the same verifier as app lock for each reveal, with no cached global reveal grant and no unlocking of the app or other messages; click mode avoids unnecessary identity authentication.
The original session, local user and participant runtime remain admitted after asynchronous authentication, including runtime identity replacement; stale work cannot return data to another owner.
Lock revision changes invalidate pending work even if the app was subsequently unlocked, and current policy/retention are checked before returning the exact requested content.

Ordinary host history/event projections and notifications remain redacted for protected text and images; native authentication behavior and browser mocks are not falsely described as equivalent runtime evidence.

cases.name: temporary reveal has a bounded visible lifetime and releases image URLs
cases.scenario: A user opens protected text and images, waits 30 seconds, opens a second message, hides manually, changes conversation/owner, locks, blurs, unmounts, or cancels during image decoding. Authentication and decoding can finish late. Inspect the component-local reveal state and Blob lifecycle rather than inferring behavior from a shared ordinary media preview. Native macOS authentication may temporarily take focus, but a delayed background result must not become an unlimited background reveal. Screen visibility is the contract; no secure browser-memory erasure or screenshot prevention is claimed.
rubric: The card initially exposes no protected body or thumbnail, and revealing uses the exact owner-scoped text/image command rather than an ordinary cached media URL.

The visible lifetime is at most 30 seconds from actual appearance, interactions do not extend it, and clock rollback or suspended timers do not knowingly preserve a stale reveal after foreground recovery.
Manual hide, another reveal, conversation/owner change, lock/logout, blur/visibility and unmount invalidate visible and pending content; late completions cannot restore cancelled content.

Image decoding precedes the visible countdown; each successful reveal owns a local Blob URL that is revoked on concealment, failure, cancellation, unmount and stale completion, without placing revealed content in shared chat or media caches.

Native authentication focus handoff is bounded and starts the visible interval only on foreground display; inline password verification does not receive an unnecessary background-visibility exception.

cases.name: frontend send handoff preserves protection and a single retry owner
cases.scenario: The sender chooses click/authenticate for a text reply or images acquired through picker, paste, drop and screenshot. A multi-image acquisition is partially accepted, later items fail, the composer resets after acceptance, and the user edits or switches conversation while staging or retrying. Trace the acquired batch's captured policy through durable outgoing admission and retry payloads. Existing ordinary sends must stay ordinary. The selected policy must apply to the entire captured batch even if the first item resets the visible composer; no remaining image or failed retry may silently downgrade. This case evaluates frontend ownership, policy propagation and the typed IPC call boundary. The separate MT-PROTECTED-006 case evaluates native durable acceptance and temporary-file authority; do not treat frontend invoke calls as native runtime proof.
rubric: Text/reply and all supported image acquisition routes capture intended protection and forward the captured owner and policy through the typed IPC boundary; failed-send retry retains that policy and unsupported protected attachments fail explicitly.

A batch snapshots its policy once, including staged screenshots, so partial acceptance and composer reset cannot downgrade remaining items; already accepted items are not resent when retrying the rejected remainder.

Normal mode resets only on successful acceptance under the original draft revision/owner, and stale completion cannot erase a newer edit, affect another conversation, or reset an unrelated policy selection.

Optimistic and canonical cards remain content-free for protected sends; accepted intent payloads do not retain protected plaintext or local image paths unnecessarily, while failed intents retain what the established retry lifecycle requires.

Frontend size/format rejection, temporary-source handoff and stale acquisition respect the captured owner/conversation. Refusal before intent transfer leaves the composer responsible; after transfer exactly one outgoing bubble owns retry, without silently using the ordinary send API.

cases.name: native protected admission preserves durable policy and temporary retry sources
cases.scenario: A captured desktop owner sends protected account/channel text replies or raster images. The session locks or retires during staging, core admission fails, or accepted work is still awaiting network delivery. Review the native IPC and its supplied core owners for durable policy persistence and temporary-source lifecycle. This case supplies native admission authority separately from the frontend retry lifecycle in MT-PROTECTED-005. Judge production authority and supported-client presentation guarantees; do not require screenshots, physical authentication evidence or modified-client resistance from this source review.
rubric: Owner-scoped text/reply and image commands preserve click/authenticate policy in authenticated core bodies or manifests and return an exact durable accepted event identity.
The original desktop session/runtime authority is rechecked at the actual core commit seam; stale ownership or app lock cannot authorize a new protected send.
Accepted identity is distinct from network delivery; an unaccepted operation cannot be reported as durable acceptance solely because staging or optimistic UI succeeded.
Protected image sends enforce the existing raster-image and size boundary, reject unsupported inputs explicitly, and never downgrade a selected protected send to the ordinary path.

Managed temporary inputs remain available after failed admission for the sole outgoing retry owner, while successful durable acceptance cleans them; ordinary user-selected source files are not deleted.
